articles.title: Serpin A1 Cargo Within Tumour-Derived Extracellular Vesicles Supports Pro-Tumoural Bias of Neutrophils in Cancer.
articles.abstract: Tumour-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) or exosomes are critical mediators of the cancer-immune system crosstalk, yet the mechanisms by which they reprogram neutrophil function in vivo remain insufficiently characterised. Here, we identify the serine protease inhibitor Serpin A1 as a predominant cargo component of small EVs (sEVs) released by head and neck cancer cels (HNC) and show that this molecule is both necessary and sufficient to confer a stable pro-tumoural programming of neutrophils. Uptake of Serpin A1-enriched sEVs elicits extensive proteomic remodelling in neutrophils including activation of STAT3 signalling, leading to sustained induction of PD-L1, increased Arginase 1 production and prolonged neutrophil lifespan. Functionally, these reprogrammed neutrophils acquire a capacity to drive epithelial-mesenchymal transition in tumour cells, and to impose exhaustion of T cells via metabolic restriction and arginine depletion, leading to their reduced cytotoxicity. Genetic ablation of Serpin A1 from tumour-derived sEVs or pharmacologic inhibition of serpin-STAT3 axis restores neutrophil anti-tumour functions. Collectively, these findings delineate a Serpin A1-STAT3/Arginase 1 as an important signalling pathway through which tumour-derived sEVs promote neutrophil-dependent immune suppression and tumour progression, and highlight EV-associated serpins as potential targets for future therapeutic intervention in cancer.

articles.title: A Review of Osteosarcoma-Derived Exosomes in Tumor Progression, Chemoresistance, and Bone Regeneration, and Their Potential in Drug Delivery.
articles.abstract: Exosomes, as critical mediators of intercellular communication, transport nucleic acids, proteins, and lipids that drive osteosarcoma (OS) progression and dynamically remodel the tumor microenvironment. Their distinctive biological properties-including low immunogenicity, high stability, and inherent targeting capability-position them as versatile tools across the entire OS management continuum, from early non-invasive diagnosis via liquid biopsy to targeted biotherapy and postoperative bone regeneration through coordinated osteogenesis-angiogenesis coupling. This review first outlines the epidemiological features and principal clinical bottlenecks of OS, then systematically summarizes exosome biogenesis, cellular uptake mechanisms, and the key molecular pathways through which exosomal cargoes regulate OS malignancy. We highlight emerging evidence that exosomal biomarkers enable real-time disease monitoring and that engineered exosomes serve as precision nanocarriers for therapeutic delivery. Notably, we emphasize recent insights into exosome-mediated crosstalk with immune cells within the osteoimmune microenvironment, their role in orchestrating vascularized bone formation, and advances in exosome-functionalized biomaterial scaffolds that effectively bridge tissue engineering with oncology. The clinical relevance of these findings lies in their potential integration into a unified diagnostic-therapeutic-regenerative paradigm, which may help overcome current limitations in surgical outcomes and chemoresistance. Nevertheless, clinical translation remains hindered by persistent challenges, including the lack of standardized isolation and characterization protocols, suboptimal in vivo delivery efficiency, batch-to-batch variability, and insufficient long-term safety data. Addressing these obstacles will require further mechanistic studies and multicenter clinical trials to establish robust regulatory frameworks. This article aims to review the roles of osteosarcoma-derived exosomes in tumor progression, chemoresistance, and bone regeneration, as well as their potential for drug delivery.

articles.title: Pantethine Restores Epidermal Homeostasis and Modulates Vesicle-Associated Proteins in Psoriasis.
articles.abstract: Psoriasis is a chronic inflammatory skin disease characterized by disrupted epidermal homeostasis driven by interconnected immuno-inflammatory, metabolic, and redox signalling networks. Vesicle-associated intercellular communication has emerged as an important contributor to inflammatory amplification and tissue remodelling within the epidermal microenvironment. Pantethine, a stable vitamin B5 derivative with lipid-modulatory and anti-inflammatory properties, has been implicated in regulation of cellular stress responses and membrane-associated signalling pathways, suggesting potential therapeutic relevance in psoriasis. Here, we investigated the effects of pantethine using a full-thickness 3D human psoriatic skin model following keratinocyte safety assessment. Integrated histopathological, immunohistochemical, quantitative RT-PCR, and proteomic analyses were employed to interrogate inflammatory, oxidative, proliferative, apoptotic, differentiation-associated and vesicle-related responses. Pantethine significantly reduced epidermal thickening and normalized multiple psoriasis-associated molecular signatures. Proteomic profiling revealed coordinated modulation of vesicle-associated, cytoskeletal and extracellular matrix-related proteins, accompanied by reduced expression of exosome-associated markers CD63 and CD9. Pantethine suppressed pro-inflammatory signalling involving IL-1β, TNF-α, IL-17, S100 family members, and hyperproliferative keratin-associated pathways while reducing caspase-3-associated apoptotic activity. Concurrently, pantethine enhanced antioxidative and immunoregulatory responses through activation of Nrf-2 and TGF-β, restored differentiation and barrier-related markers including filaggrin, caspase-14, and involucrin, and reduced hypoxia- and tissue-remodelling-associated mediators including HIF-1α, VEGF, COL6A3, and COL1A2. Network-based proteomic analyses further identified computationally inferred associations with SLIT/ROBO-related pathways, although these associations require further functional validation. Collectively, these findings support pantethine as a promising candidate that modulates vesicle-associated proteins together with inflammatory and tissue-remodelling responses involved in epidermal homeostasis.

articles.title: Microneedle-Delivered Plant-Derived Exosome-like Nanovesicles for Dermatological Diseases: A Comprehensive Review.
articles.abstract: Plant-derived extracellular vesicle-like nanovesicles (PELNs) are being investigated as plant-derived preparations with intrinsic bioactivity and potential utility as nanocarriers. Microneedles (MNs) can create transient skin microchannels and may support localized intradermal delivery of vesicle-containing formulations. The intersection of these approaches is promising, but the available evidence remains heterogeneous and includes direct PELN-MN studies, PELN studies without MNs, and related mammalian extracellular vesicle platforms. Here we provide a comprehensive review of PELN identity, isolation, characterization, cargo, and proposed dermatological activities, followed by an assessment of MN designs relevant to vesicle delivery. We searched PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and Embase, screened records in duplicate, and classified each included study by the directness of evidence into studies providing direct PELN-MN skin evidence, PELN evidence without MNs, mammalian extracellular vesicle MN analogue evidence, and non-dermatological or conceptual evidence. Current limitations include uncertain vesicle identity, co-isolated plant constituents, variable preparation and dosing methods, limited controls for the mechanical effects of microneedling, and incomplete clinical follow-up. Progress toward translation will require source-specific quality attributes, orthogonal potency assays, transparent comparators, and adequately controlled clinical studies.

articles.title: Functional engineering of adipose-derived stem cell exosomes and its application in soft tissue regeneration.
articles.abstract: Adipose-derived stem cell exosomes are increasingly recognized as promising cell-free mediators for soft tissue repair because of their favorable biocompatibility, low immunogenicity, and broad paracrine activity. By transferring regulatory RNAs, proteins, lipids, and other bioactive molecules, they participate in key regenerative processes, including angiogenesis, immune modulation, extracellular matrix remodeling, and cellular proliferation. However, native adipose-derived stem cell exosomes still face important translational limitations, including limited targeting specificity, variable cargo composition, rapid clearance, and insufficient retention at injured sites.

articles.title: Exosome-Based Therapies for Skin Aging: Sources, Mechanisms, and Evidence from Preclinical and Clinical Studies.
articles.abstract: Skin aging is an inevitable physiological process co-driven by endogenous genetic programs and exogenous environmental factors, characterized by the progressive deterioration of skin structure and function, which manifests as wrinkles, sagging, pigmentation, and impaired barrier function. Extracellular vesicles, particularly exosomes, are nanoscale membranous vesicles actively secreted by cells, functioning as pivotal mediators of intercellular communication through the transport of diverse bioactive molecules. Exosomes derived from diverse sources, including mesenchymal stem cells, somatic cells, plants, milk, and plasma, can effectively reverse skin aging through multiple mechanisms, such as alleviating oxidative damage, promoting collagen synthesis, inhibiting excessive expression of matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs), clearing senescent cells, and improving mitochondrial function. Additionally, engineering modifications and optimized delivery systems can further enhance the targeting ability and synergistic therapeutic efficacy of exosomes. However, the clinical application of exosomes remains constrained by exosome heterogeneity, the lack of standardized isolation and production methods, limited delivery efficiency, and insufficient long-term clinical evidence regarding safety and efficacy. This review systematically summarizes the fundamental research, mechanisms, and clinical evidence of exosomes in combating skin aging. We comprehensively explore the application prospects and challenges, emphasizing the significant values of different exosomes in combating skin aging.

articles.title: Bioactive M2 exosome hybrid nanocomposites for immune therapy of psoriasis.
articles.abstract: Psoriasis is a chronic autoimmune skin disease characterized by persistent oxidative stress and sustained inflammation, affecting approximately 1-8% of the global population, with no curative therapy has been well-established to date. To address this, we developed a bioactive hybrid nanocomposite (Exo-Ce) by chemically conjugating M2 macrophage-derived exosomes with cerium oxide nanoparticles (CeNP), which was applied for synergistic and immunomodulatory therapy of psoriasis. This nanohybrid system effectively integrates the natural immunomodulatory properties of exosomes with the reliable antioxidant enzyme-mimetic activities of CeNP. In vitro, mild thiol-maleimide click chemistry minimizes exosome damage; Exo-Ce maintains parental M2-exosome core bioactivity and exhibits ROS-scavenging capacity, significantly reducing intracellular ROS levels and suppressing the secretion of pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-6 and TNF-α). Following subcutaneous administration in an imiquimod (IMQ)-induced psoriasis mouse model, Exo-Ce markedly ameliorated psoriatic lesions, as evidenced by reduced lesional area, attenuated epidermal hyperkeratosis and acanthosis, and decreased immune cell infiltration. More specifically, Exo-Ce could promote the polarization of macrophages toward an anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype via its ROS-scavenging activity, as well as downregulate key psoriasis-associated cytokines (e.g., IL-1β and TNF-α), thereby facilitating the restoration of tissue homeostasis in vivo. Altogether, our findings position Exo-Ce as a biocompatible and synergistic nanohybrid platform for psoriasis immunotherapy, potentially offering a promising strategy for clinical translation.
